claim: card.glamourStatusDye 'TEINTES' (en 'DYES', the piece cannot take the dyes) reads as 'shades'/'dyed', not a dye problem.

sk_reason: The defect is real. packages/bot-logic/src/i18n/locales/fr.json:618 has "glamourStatusDye": "TEINTES", and glamour.ts:234 shows it as the blocked-status pill when a piece fails on dye (glamour-card.ts:278). Everywhere else in this codebase "teinte" means hue: "Teinte OKLCH" at fr.json:60, web "deltaHue": "TEINTE", and "sortHue". The house dye word is "teinture": bot fr.json:512/516/585 and web "colDye": "TEINTURE". So the pill reads as "HUES", or as the adjective "dyed", not as "won't take these dyes". I would grade it P2, not P1. This is the wrong house word for a concept, the same class as the German "FARBEN" on the same key, which the brief treats as a terminology fault (German dye = Farbstoff, never Farbe). The meaning can still be recovered: the pill is drawn in the blocked colour, and the card's footer lines explain the problem in correct French ("qui ne prend pas ces teintures" in glamourFixedDye, "ne prend pas les teintures du fichier" in glamourBlockedDye). The English "DYES" is just as terse. So this is a misleading short label with an explanation nearby, not text that is wrong with nothing to correct it. The proposed fix "TEINTURES" is correct (fitText shrinks the status column to fit). Dropping the "NON MIRAGE" half is also correct.
